We said it, we looked it, and even the boys "jollied" us as we came within the bounds of civilisation. The latter action made us bite our lips, and the color rush to our cheeks, but we had to bear these gratuitous insults without rebuke, because we knew and felt that young Australia had the best of us. The nearest "pub." had a fascination for us. We allowed ourselves to roll off our horses, and the amiable old lady who presided behind the bar soon comforted our weary spirits (we had spirits) with something enervating. And thus ended our mission to Katoomba, and glad we were that it was so. We all voted Mr. Hassall, Mr.
